subject: Transpacific region readiness — initial sizing, fallback lanes, and SOW cadence
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@cumulusai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Transpacific pilot: latency targets and dedicated ask

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CumulusAI is moving forward with a small transpacific pilot (Singapore + Tokyo presence) and we need Redwood to propose a dedicated footprint that meets these constraints:

- 99th percentile generation latency target: <220ms for 2k token prompt
- Baseline QPS: 6 sustained; peak bursts up to ~28 for 2-3 minute windows
- Data residency: customer data must remain in APAC region; SOC2 evidence requested during SOW
- Preferred HW: A100 or H100 options; open to fractional/quantized variants for cost reduction

Attached is a short requirements doc with traffic shape and model families (cumulus_transpacific_requirements.pdf).

Can you share a sizing recommendation + monthly committed pricing and proposed fallback (hosted/shared) if we exceed burst lanes? We're targeting a soft launch mid-December.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Platforms, CumulusAI
ops@cumulusai.com

[attachment: cumulus_transpacific_requirements.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Transpacific pilot: latency targets and dedicated ask

Sara — really appreciate the detail. Looping in Irene (capacity planning) and Jordan (SOW/procurement) to scope a recommended starting pool and pricing cadence.

Initial asks for our side:

- Any hard SLA/credits requirement for launch?

Irene/Jordan — please see attached reqs. Quick aim: a modest dedicated pool + burst overlay, and a playbook for emergency crossover to hosted. Expect we’ll need a 90-day commit to justify initial node reservation.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@cumulusai.com>
Date: 2027-10-31T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transpacific pilot: latency targets and dedicated ask — sizing proposal

Sean / team / Sara —

Quick sizing note after a first-pass simulation (attached: redwood_sizing_calc_v1.xlsx):

Recommendation (Phase 1 — 90 day pilot):
- Dedicated pool: 8x A100 (80GB) nodes configured for continuous batching + KV prefix caching.
- Burst overlay: allow up to 8 additional on-demand nodes (hosted or cloud-burst) for short peaks.
- If low-latency <170ms is required for 99th: consider swapping 4x A100 for 4x H100-like instances (adds ~25% infra cost).
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization validated for your model family can reduce token cost ~35% with minimal regen quality loss for common prompts; we should A/B a small eval set.

Cost / commit: rough sticker (USD, monthly amortized)
- 8x A100 reserved: $64,000/mo (3-month commit)
- Burst buffer (on-demand): metered at $10 / node-hr billed usage
- H100 config delta: +25% to monthly reserved line item

Operational notes:
- We’ll include an automatic fallback policy routing overflow to hosted TPU pools, with throttling and graceful degrade messages.
- SOC2 artifacts + region control will be included in the SOW; Jordan will own formal evidence bundling.

Attachments: redwood_sizing_calc_v1.xlsx (nodes, simulated p95/p99, cost assumptions)

Irene Choi
Head, Capacity & Onboarding, Redwood Inference

Sara
